theAmbiguityAcknowledged.whyTheyConflict: SD3 reads as one shared deduplicated pool, while SD7 resolves each near-duplicate pair by the rank of the sample being drawn. SET_P and SET_R have different ranks, so one shared final survivor set cannot honour SD7's per-sample rank for both samples at once. SD9 then counts pages 'after SD7 deduplication' without saying which sample's survivors it counts.
theAmbiguityAcknowledged.staleCrossReferenceNoted: SD3's SET_P clause cites '(SD6)' for deduplication, but deduplication is rule SD7. The cross-reference is noted here and deliberately NOT edited: R3 bytes are frozen.
